stem: A ticketing company is building an order system for customers in North America, Europe and Asia. It needs a relational schema with SQL, transactions that are strongly consistent everywhere, and write capacity that grows by adding resources rather than by moving to a bigger single primary server. Which database should the team choose?

choices.text: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with cross-region read replicas, which serve reads close to users while one primary takes all writes
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL with read pool instances, which add read nodes on demand while the cluster stays in a single region
Spanner with a multi-region instance configuration, which shards data automatically and keeps transactions strongly consistent
Bigtable with clusters in three regions and replication, which spreads reads and writes across clusters in every continent

stem: An energy company collects a reading every few seconds from two million smart meters. The application writes very high volumes of small records and reads them back by meter ID and time range with single-digit millisecond latency. The developers already use the Apache HBase API. Which service fits best?

choices.text: Firestore, with one document per reading stored in a collection per meter and a composite index on the timestamp field
Bigtable, with a row key that starts with the meter ID followed by a timestamp so each meter's readings sit together
BigQuery, with a table partitioned by day and clustered by meter ID so that range scans on recent readings stay quick
Cloud SQL for MySQL, with a table indexed on meter ID and timestamp and several read replicas for the dashboard queries

stem: A firm is moving an internal finance application from its data center to Google Cloud. The application uses Microsoft SQL Server, and the team wants Google to handle backups, patching and high availability failover without changing the database engine. Which service should they use?

choices.text: Cloud SQL for SQL Server, a managed instance that keeps the same engine and adds automated backups and a standby for failover
BigQuery with a dataset per database, a managed warehouse that runs the application's T-SQL transactions without changes
Spanner with the GoogleSQL dialect, a managed database whose schema accepts SQL Server tables after a direct backup restore
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, a managed cluster whose engine takes SQL Server queries after the schema is imported unchanged

stem: A retailer's order application runs on PostgreSQL. Managers want reports that run heavy analytical queries directly on the live order data, without a nightly export, and without slowing down the order transactions. The team wants to keep using standard PostgreSQL clients. Which service should the team choose?

choices.text: Bigtable, with the order data copied into it so that reports can scan wide rows by order date with low latency
Memorystore for Redis, with report results cached in memory so that repeated analytical queries return quickly
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, with a scheduled export to Cloud Storage and a BigQuery load job that runs every night
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, using its columnar engine and read pool instances to run the analytical queries on live data

stem: A start-up is building a mobile and web app that stores user profiles and posts as JSON-like documents. The team wants a serverless database that scales automatically without capacity planning, charges for actual use, and works with the Firebase SDKs. Which database should they pick?

choices.text: Bigtable, a wide-column database whose cluster nodes are sized up front and adjusted when traffic changes
Memorystore for Redis, an in-memory store whose hashes hold each profile and post as a set of key fields
Firestore, a serverless document database that scales automatically and integrates with the Firebase platform
Cloud SQL for MySQL, a relational instance with a JSON column type and storage that grows automatically

stem: Analysts at a media company need to run ad hoc SQL queries over several hundred terabytes of clickstream data and connect a BI tool to the results. The team does not want to provision, patch or scale any database servers. Which service should hold the data?

choices.text: Spanner, with a regional instance configuration whose compute capacity is raised before the reporting runs
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, with the largest machine type and read replicas added for each group of analysts
Bigtable, with an instance cluster sized for the full data set and its nodes scaled out during peak query hours
BigQuery, a serverless data warehouse that separates storage from compute and runs SQL queries without servers

stem: A web application on Compute Engine stores user sessions in a Cloud SQL database, and page loads slow down under heavy traffic. The developers already use an open source Redis client library and want a managed in-memory store that answers in under a millisecond, reached over a private IP in their VPC. What should they use?

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, a managed Redis-protocol store that the existing client can use with no code changes
Firestore in Native mode, a managed document store that the existing client reaches through its MongoDB API
A Cloud SQL read replica, a managed copy of the database that the existing client reaches over the same private IP
Bigtable with an SSD cluster, a managed wide-column store that the existing client reaches through its HBase API

stem: A logistics company runs dozens of services that produce and consume events with Apache Kafka client libraries and Kafka Connect, on a self-managed cluster. They want Google Cloud to run the cluster for them without rewriting producers or consumers. Which service should they choose?

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, whose streams store the events and accept the existing Kafka producer calls with no code changes
Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka, which runs Kafka clusters that the existing Kafka clients connect to
Pub/Sub, whose topics and subscriptions receive the existing Kafka producer and consumer calls with no code changes
Dataflow, whose streaming jobs act as Kafka brokers that the existing Kafka clients connect to as their bootstrap servers

stem: A game studio wants to collect gameplay events from thousands of game servers, enrich and aggregate them in near real time, and write the results into BigQuery. The team wants fully managed services with no clusters to run. Which TWO services should they combine? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, to hold the raw events in memory and run the enrichment and aggregation step in the cache
Filestore, to collect the events as files on a shared NFS share that BigQuery reads directly as the source table
Dataflow, to run a streaming Apache Beam pipeline that reads the events, transforms them and writes to BigQuery
Cloud SQL for MySQL, to stage every raw event in a table and run scheduled stored procedures that load BigQuery
Pub/Sub, to receive the events asynchronously from the game servers and buffer them for downstream processing

stem: A media team runs a rendering application on a managed instance group of Linux VMs and on a GKE cluster. All VMs and Pods must read and write the same POSIX file tree at the same time over NFS, with file locking. Which storage should the team provision?

choices.text: A Cloud Storage bucket mounted with Cloud Storage FUSE, which provides file locking and full POSIX semantics
A Filestore instance, whose NFS file share every VM and Pod can mount read-write at the same time
A Memorystore for Redis instance, whose keys each hold one file so that every VM and Pod reads the same data
A zonal Persistent Disk attached to every VM, which mounts it read-write as a shared POSIX file system

stem: An engineering firm is moving Windows file servers to Google Cloud. Users on Windows desktops map the shares as network drives over SMB, and Linux build servers mount other volumes over NFS. The firm wants one fully managed service that provides both protocols. Which service should they choose?

choices.text: Google Cloud Managed Lustre, mounting its parallel file system on both the Windows desktops and the build servers
Cloud Storage with Cloud Storage FUSE, mounting each bucket as a network drive on the Windows desktops over SMB
Filestore, using the regional tier for continuous availability and mounting the shares from Windows over SMB
Google Cloud NetApp Volumes, which provides managed volumes over SMB and NFS protocols with snapshots and backups

stem: A research lab trains large machine learning models on hundreds of GPU VMs and GKE nodes. Training needs a shared POSIX file system that delivers very high aggregate throughput and IOPS to all nodes at once, and data sets are staged from Cloud Storage. Which storage service is designed for this?

choices.text: Google Cloud Managed Lustre, a fully managed parallel file system for AI and HPC with transfers to and from Cloud Storage
Cloud Storage with the Nearline storage class, a bucket that every GPU node reads through the JSON API during training
Filestore with the basic tier, a legacy managed NFS share for basic file sharing that every GPU node mounts at once
Memorystore for Redis with five replicas, an in-memory store whose keys hold the training files for every GPU node

stem: A finance team continuously uploads transaction exports to a bucket and runs an analysis job on them about once a month. The files must stay online with fast access, and the team wants to lower at-rest storage cost without paying for retrievals more often than needed. Which storage class should the bucket use by default?

choices.text: Standard storage, which is meant for data read less than once a year and has a 365-day minimum storage duration
Nearline storage, which is meant for data read or modified about once a month and has a 30-day minimum storage duration
Archive storage, which is meant for data read about once a month and has offline retrieval that takes several hours
Coldline storage, which is meant for data read or modified several times every week and has no minimum storage duration

stem: A hospital must keep scanned records for ten years for regulatory reasons. The records are almost never read, but during an audit some files must be readable at once. The team is evaluating Archive storage. Which TWO statements about Archive storage are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An object deleted or replaced before it has been stored for 365 days is charged as if it was stored for 365 days
Objects in Archive storage must first be restored to Standard storage, which can take several hours per object
Archive storage can be used only in single-region buckets, so it cannot be combined with dual-region redundancy
Archive storage cannot be set as a bucket's default class, so each object must get the class when it is uploaded
Objects in Archive storage are readable within milliseconds, with no restore step before the data can be accessed

stem: A bucket holds 2 TB of log files in Standard storage. An engineer changes the bucket's default storage class to Coldline to save money, but a week later every existing object still shows the Standard class. What explains this, and how can the engineer change the existing objects?

choices.text: The default class is ignored while uniform bucket-level access is on; disable it so the existing objects can take the new default class
The change takes up to 30 days to reach existing objects; wait for the background conversion to finish before checking the class again
The bucket is in a multi-region, where Coldline is not supported; recreate the bucket in a single region and then copy the objects there
The default class applies only to objects added later; rewrite the existing objects with gcloud storage objects update and --storage-class

stem: An engineer must upload a local directory of about 200 GB with many subdirectories from a workstation into gs://proj-media-raw, keeping the folder structure, and the objects should be stored as Nearline. The network link is good. Which command is the simplest correct choice?

choices.text: bq load --source_format=CSV proj_media.raw ./media/* --storage_class=NEARLINE
gcloud storage cp ./media gs://proj-media-raw --no-clobber --storage-class=NEARLINE
gcloud storage cp --recursive ./media gs://proj-media-raw --storage-class=NEARLINE
gcloud storage buckets create gs://proj-media-raw --placement=./media --default-storage-class=NEARLINE

stem: A company keeps 400 TB of product images in Amazon S3 and wants to move them to Cloud Storage, then copy new and changed files every night until the cut-over. The team wants a managed service that retries failures and checks integrity, without writing scripts or running copy servers. What should they use?

choices.text: A BigQuery load job from the S3 bucket each night, followed by an export of the loaded data to Cloud Storage
A Compute Engine VM that runs gcloud storage rsync from the S3 bucket every night through a cron job on the VM
Storage Transfer Service, with an S3 source, a Cloud Storage destination and a daily schedule for the transfer job
Transfer Appliance, shipped to the S3 region so that the images are copied onto it and loaded into Cloud Storage

stem: An analyst runs bq load to load CSV files from gs://acme-sales-us/2026/*.csv into the table sales.daily. The bucket is in the US multi-region, and the sales dataset was created in the europe-west1 region. The load job fails before reading any rows. What is the most likely cause and fix?

choices.text: The bucket and dataset are in different locations; copy the files to a bucket colocated with the dataset, or load into a dataset in the bucket's location
The table needs an explicit schema file for CSV loads; pass a local JSON schema file because schema auto-detection cannot read CSV
The analyst needs Storage Transfer Service between Cloud Storage and BigQuery; create a transfer job, because bq load cannot read buckets
Wildcards are not supported in Cloud Storage URIs for bq load; list every CSV file by name in a comma-separated list of URIs instead

stem: Each night a job drops a CSV file with one header row into gs://acme-orders/daily/. An engineer writes a bq load command that adds the file's rows to the existing table orders.history, which has a schema and holds years of data that must not be lost. Which TWO choices must the command make? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Pass --time_partitioning_type=DAY on each run so that the existing table is converted to daily partitions
Pass --source_format=NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON so that the header line is read as the names of the columns
Pass --replace so that the existing schema is kept and new rows are written alongside the old data
Use --skip_leading_rows=1 so that the header row is not loaded as a data row into the table
Append the rows, by passing --noreplace or by leaving out --replace, so that existing rows stay

stem: A payments company stores transaction receipts in Cloud Storage. The bucket must keep serving reads and writes with the same bucket name if one region goes down, the data must stay in two regions the company chooses, and newly written objects must be copied to the second region within 15 minutes. Which TWO settings meet these needs when the bucket is created? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A single-region location, with Autoclass enabled so that objects move to colder classes in a second region over time
The recovery point objective set to ASYNC_TURBO, which turns on turbo replication for the dual-region bucket
A multi-region location such as EU, with turbo replication enabled so that copies reach a second region in minutes
A single-region location, with Object Versioning enabled so that earlier versions of objects can be restored later
A dual-region location, either a predefined pair or a configurable dual-region whose two regions are set with --placement

stem: A logistics company is moving a legacy inventory application to Google Cloud. The application runs on a commercial Linux distribution, loads a vendor-supplied kernel driver at boot, and the vendor supports it only when it runs unmodified on a full operating system. The team wants to change as little as possible. Where should the team run the application?

choices.text: On a GKE Autopilot cluster, running the application as a Deployment with the vendor driver installed through an init container in each Pod
On Cloud Run, after packaging the application and its kernel driver into a container image that loads the driver when each instance starts
On Cloud Run functions, splitting the application into event-driven functions that call the vendor driver through a shared library at runtime
On Compute Engine VMs built from an image of that distribution, so the team controls the operating system, kernel modules and installed packages

stem: A small team has a stateless REST API packaged as a container image. It receives traffic only during office hours and none at night or on weekends. The team does not want to manage VMs or clusters and does not want to pay for compute while the API is idle. Which compute option should the team choose?

choices.text: A Cloud Run service deployed from the image, letting it scale to zero instances when no requests arrive
A regional managed instance group of small VMs running the container, autoscaled on average CPU utilization with a minimum of zero
A GKE Standard cluster with the cluster autoscaler enabled on its node pool, running the image as a Deployment behind a Service
An Agent Runtime deployment on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, which runs the image in a fully managed environment

stem: A developer has built a customer-support AI agent and now needs to run it in production. The team wants a fully managed environment that deploys and scales the agent, keeps conversation state across turns, can store long-term memories about users, and provides tracing and logging, without the team operating servers. Which option fits best?

choices.text: Split each agent tool into a separate Cloud Run function and keep the conversation history in the instance memory of each function
Deploy the agent to Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and use Agent Platform Sessions and Memory Bank for state
Package the agent as a container and run it on a Compute Engine managed instance group, storing session state in a Cloud SQL database the team manages
Run the agent on a GKE Standard cluster with a StatefulSet that stores each conversation on the Persistent Disk of its Pod

stem: An engineer created a reporting VM with a script copied from an old wiki that included --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE and --no-restart-on-failure. Last night Google performed host maintenance, and this morning the VM is in the TERMINATED state and nobody restarted it. The VM uses a general-purpose machine type with no GPUs. How should the engineer change the VM's host maintenance policy?

choices.text: Enable deletion protection on the VM so that Compute Engine can no longer stop or terminate it during host maintenance events
Recreate the VM as a Spot VM so that Compute Engine moves it to another host automatically whenever maintenance is scheduled
Set the maintenance behavior to migrate (live migration) and turn automatic restart back on so host errors also restart the VM
Add a snapshot schedule to the boot disk so that the VM is recreated from the latest snapshot after each maintenance event

stem: A data team plans to use Spot VMs to cut the cost of a nightly transcoding fleet. Which statements about Spot VMs are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Spot VMs are covered by the Compute Engine SLA at a reduced uptime percentage, so short outages caused by preemption earn service credits
Spot VMs are priced by bidding: you set a maximum hourly bid, and the VM is preempted whenever the market price rises above your bid
Spot VMs cannot live migrate during host maintenance and cannot be configured to restart automatically when a host event occurs
Spot VMs keep running for at most 24 hours, after which Compute Engine always stops them, even when spare capacity is still available
Compute Engine can preempt a Spot VM at any time to reclaim capacity, and its termination action decides whether the VM is stopped or deleted

stem: A media startup renders video frames pulled from a work queue. Each frame is independent and can simply be retried, and the goal is the lowest compute cost. When Compute Engine reclaims a worker VM, the team wants a replacement worker created automatically from the same configuration without anyone stepping in. What should the team set up?

choices.text: Standard VMs on a sole-tenant node group, with the automatic restart policy enabled so that crashed workers come back
An unmanaged instance group of Spot VMs, each created by hand, with a load balancer health check pointed at the group
One large Spot VM with automatic restart turned on, so that Compute Engine restarts it on another host after preemption
A managed instance group whose instance template uses the Spot provisioning model, so the group recreates preempted VMs

stem: A team creates Spot VMs each night with gcloud compute instances create ... --provisioning-model=SPOT. After preemptions, dozens of VMs remain in the TERMINATED state, and their boot disks keep adding to the bill. The team wants preempted VMs to disappear on their own. Which change should they make to the create command?

choices.text: Add --no-restart-on-failure so that Compute Engine does not try to bring the Spot VM back after it is preempted
Add --instance-termination-action=DELETE so that Compute Engine deletes each Spot VM when it preempts it
Replace --provisioning-model=SPOT with --preemptible so that preempted VMs are removed after 24 hours of running
Add --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE so that preempted VMs are terminated permanently instead of only stopped

stem: A finance team runs a third-party risk engine licensed per vCPU; they own licenses for exactly 6 vCPUs. Load tests show the engine needs 6 vCPUs and about 30 GB of memory. The closest predefined type, n2-standard-8, would need 8 licenses. What should the cloud engineer create?

choices.text: A VM with an N2 custom machine type of 6 vCPUs and 30 GB of memory
A VM with the predefined n2-highmem-4 machine type and 32 GB of memory
A VM with a C3 custom machine type of 6 vCPUs and 30 GB of memory
A VM on a sole-tenant node with 8 vCPUs, reserving 2 vCPUs for later

stem: An in-memory analytics product is licensed per vCPU, and the team has budgeted for 4 vCPUs. The data set needs 64 GB of RAM on a single VM, and CPU usage is low. The team plans to use the N2 machine series. Which configuration meets both constraints?

choices.text: The predefined n2-highmem-8 type with 8 vCPUs and 64 GB, then license only 4 of the vCPUs in the product
An N2 custom machine type with 4 vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, created with the extended memory feature
An E2 custom machine type with 4 vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, since E2 has no memory-per-vCPU limit
An N2 custom machine type with 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of memory, the most memory a 4-vCPU custom type allows

stem: A team runs a self-managed PostgreSQL server on one Compute Engine VM in us-central1-a. Management now requires that the database survive the loss of that zone with no loss of committed data, and a standby VM can be kept stopped in us-central1-b. Which storage design meets the requirement?

choices.text: Keep the data on a zonal Hyperdisk Balanced volume with a snapshot schedule every hour, and create a new disk in us-central1-b from the latest snapshot
Keep the data on a zonal Hyperdisk Balanced volume with Asynchronous Replication to europe-west1, and fail over to a VM created in that region
Keep the data on Local SSD disks in RAID 0 for speed, and copy the database files to a Cloud Storage bucket in the same region every fifteen minutes
Keep the data on a Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability or regional Persistent Disk volume replicated to both zones, and attach it to the standby VM on failover

stem: A MySQL VM keeps 400 GB of data on a balanced Persistent Disk and is limited by disk IOPS. To get the IOPS it needs, the team would have to grow the disk to several terabytes it will never fill. The VM's machine series supports Hyperdisk. Which option raises IOPS without paying for unused capacity?

choices.text: Move the data to a Hyperdisk Throughput volume and raise its IOPS level separately from its size
Resize the balanced Persistent Disk to several terabytes, since disk IOPS scale with its capacity
Move the data to a Hyperdisk Balanced volume and set the provisioned IOPS independently of its size
Move the data to Local SSD disks, which deliver higher IOPS than any network-attached disk type

stem: An inference fleet of 400 Compute Engine VMs must load the same 150 GB of model weights at startup. The weights never change between releases, and startup time matters. The team wants one copy of the data that every VM reads directly as a disk. Which disk type should they use?

choices.text: A Hyperdisk ML volume, loaded once and then attached in read-only mode to every VM in the fleet
A Hyperdisk Balanced volume in multi-writer mode, attached to every VM in the fleet at the same time
A Hyperdisk Throughput volume, attached to one VM that copies the weights to the others over the network
A Hyperdisk Extreme volume, attached in read-write mode to every VM in the fleet for the highest IOPS

stem: A team plans to add Local SSD to a Microsoft SQL Server VM. Which statements about Local SSD are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Local SSD cannot be used as a boot volume, so the VM still needs a durable boot disk such as Hyperdisk or Persistent Disk
Local SSD is synchronously replicated to a second zone, so its data survives the failure of the zone that hosts the VM
Local SSD data is kept when a Spot VM is preempted, because the disks stay attached to the stopped VM on the same host
Local SSD disks can be detached from a running VM and attached to another VM in the same zone, like a Hyperdisk volume
Local SSD gives the fastest block storage but is temporary, so it suits scratch data and caches such as SQL Server tempdb

stem: A web tier runs in a managed instance group created from the instance template web-tmpl-v1, which uses e2-medium. The team wants new and existing VMs to use n2-standard-2, but finds no way to edit the machine type of web-tmpl-v1. What is the correct approach?

choices.text: Delete web-tmpl-v1 while the group is still using it, then recreate a template with the same name and the new machine type
Run gcloud compute instance-templates update web-tmpl-v1 with the new machine type, then restart the VMs in the group one by one
Stop each VM in the group, change its machine type to n2-standard-2 directly, and start it again so the template no longer matters
Create a new template, such as web-tmpl-v2 based on the old one with n2-standard-2, and roll it out to the group with an update

stem: A managed instance group autoscales on average CPU utilization with a 60% target. Each new VM spends about 4 minutes installing packages at boot, with high CPU, before the app serves traffic. During every spike the group overshoots and adds far more VMs than needed. Which autoscaler setting should be adjusted?

choices.text: Configure scale-in controls with a small maximum allowed reduction, so that the group adds fewer VMs during each spike
Set the initialization period to about 240 seconds, so that scale-out ignores data from VMs that are still starting up
Raise the target CPU utilization to 95%, so that the high CPU of booting VMs no longer triggers additional scale-out
Set the stabilization period to 4 minutes, so that the autoscaler waits that long before it adds any new VMs to the group

stem: Workers in a managed instance group process messages from a Pub/Sub subscription. The group autoscales on average CPU utilization, and the team set the minimum number of instances to 0 so it would be empty overnight when the queue is empty, yet at least one VM always keeps running. How should the team reach zero instances when there is no work?

choices.text: Switch the signal to HTTP load balancing serving capacity, which reports zero usage once all requests have stopped
Add a scaling schedule with a capacity of 0 instances every night, which forces the group to delete all of its VMs
Scale on a Cloud Monitoring metric for the subscription's backlog of undelivered messages instead of CPU, keeping minimum at 0
Lower the CPU utilization target to 1%, so that the autoscaler sees even one idle VM as over target and removes it

stem: A retailer's web tier runs on Compute Engine. It must keep serving if an entire zone in us-east1 goes down, and VMs on which the web application has hung (while the VM itself still runs) must be replaced automatically. Which configuration meets these goals? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Configure application-based autohealing with a health check on the app's endpoint, so the group recreates unhealthy VMs
Rely on the load balancer's health check alone, since a failing backend health check makes the group recreate the VM
Keep automatic restart enabled in the VMs' host maintenance policy, so that Compute Engine restarts VMs whose app hangs
Put the VMs in an unmanaged instance group that contains VMs from all three zones of us-east1 behind the load balancer
Create a regional managed instance group so that the group's VMs are spread across several zones of us-east1

stem: A project's Linux VMs use SSH keys stored in project metadata. The security team wants contractors to get SSH access through IAM, without sudo, and to lose access automatically as soon as their IAM role is removed. Which actions should the cloud engineer take? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add each contractor's public SSH key to the project metadata and set an expiry time on every key that is added
Set the metadata key enable-oslogin to TRUE in the project metadata so that the project's VMs use OS Login
Grant the contractors the roles/compute.osAdminLogin role so that they can log in to the VMs through OS Login
Grant the contractors the roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 role so that they can manage SSH keys on the instances
Grant the contractors the roles/compute.osLogin role on the project or on the specific VMs they need to reach

stem: A project still uses metadata-based SSH keys, and a dozen administrators have their keys in project metadata. One new VM processes payroll data and must accept only the two keys that the payroll team adds to that VM's own metadata. OS Login cannot be used yet. What should the engineer configure on the VM?

choices.text: Remove the dozen administrator keys from the project metadata, and add the two payroll keys to the project metadata instead
Create the payroll VM without a service account, so that the keys stored in project metadata are not copied onto the VM
Set the metadata key block-project-ssh-keys to TRUE on the payroll VM, and add the two payroll keys to its instance metadata
Set the metadata key enable-oslogin to FALSE on the payroll VM, so that it reads only the keys stored in its own metadata

stem: An operations team set up VM Manager and a weekly patch deployment for 200 Ubuntu VMs. Patch compliance reports show up for every VM, but patch jobs fail on the VMs that have no external IP address; their subnet has no Cloud NAT and no proxy. What should the team do?

choices.text: Grant the OS Config agent's service account the Compute Admin role on the project, so it can download patches for the VMs
Recreate the failing VMs with external IP addresses, since VM Manager requires every managed VM to have a public address
Switch the patch deployment to OS inventory management, which installs updates without contacting package repositories
Give the VMs a path to package updates, such as Cloud NAT for the subnet or a local repository the VMs can reach

stem: A security team requires that a specific monitoring package be installed on every Linux VM labeled env=prod, and that it be reinstalled automatically if someone removes it. The team wants to use a VM Manager feature rather than writing its own tooling. Which feature should it use?

choices.text: OS policies, which describe the desired package state for the selected VMs and keep that state in place
A startup script in the instance metadata of each production VM that installs the package at every boot
OS inventory management, which collects and reports which packages are present on each selected VM
Patch deployments, which apply operating system updates to the selected VMs on a recurring schedule

stem: A research group will train a large recommendation model. The model is dominated by matrix multiplications, uses ultra-large embeddings, has no custom operations in its training loop, and is expected to train for weeks with large batch sizes. Which hardware should the cloud engineer plan for?

choices.text: GPUs attached to Compute Engine VMs, because GPUs are the only accelerator that Google Cloud offers for model training
High-CPU Compute Engine VMs, because large embeddings run best on general-purpose CPUs with plenty of cores
Cloud TPUs, because they suit models whose training loop relies on many custom PyTorch operations run on CPUs
Cloud TPUs, because they are ASICs built for large matrix operations and suit large models that train for weeks
